number noun

also numbers, how many, a number of

classical

Cic. Rep. 6.18 (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Germ. 11.2
Traupman 39: telephone number numerus

numerus, numerī m.

noun, second declension

A number and a count alike, also the number of a telephone (Traupman). “A number of” is aliquot or complūrēs, not numerus.

Examples

  • nec diērum numerum, ut nōs, sed noctium computant

    they count the number not of days, as we do, but of nightsTac. Germ. 11.2

  • convīvārum numerum incipere oportēre ā Grātiārum numerō et prōgredī ad Mūsārum

    that the number of guests should begin at the number of the Graces and go up to that of the MusesGell. 13.11.2

See also count, arithmetic, total.
